sections.h2: Where can I pay a Washington County property tax bill?
sections.html:
Property Records and Taxpayer Services runs the tax counter at the Government Center, 14949 62nd Street North in Stillwater, with a phone line at 651-430-6175. Mail goes to PO Box 200, Stillwater, MN 55082-0200 and has to be postmarked by the due date. The property tax page adds online payment by e-check (a $0.75 fee) or card (2.35%, with a $1.49 minimum), plus bank bill pay.

Owners in the south or north of the county need not drive to Stillwater, because tax payments are taken at the Government Center and at each service center:

  • Government Center in Stillwater
  • Central Service Center, 1261 Woodlane Drive, Woodbury
  • Cottage Grove Service Center, 13000 Ravine Parkway
  • Headwaters Service Center, 19955 Forest Road North, Forest Lake

The department warns that boxes are emptied the next business day, so a payment dropped after hours on the last day should not be counted on. The same office also takes homestead applications at each of those locations.

sections.h2: How does Washington County differ from its rural neighbors?
sections.html:
Washington County is the metro's eastern edge, bounded by the St. Croix River and Wisconsin. The territorial legislature created it on October 27, 1849, naming it for George Washington, and Stillwater, the seat, calls itself the Birthplace of Minnesota because of an 1848 convention held there. Logging and sawmills came first, with a mill at Marine on St. Croix in 1839. Once the forests were depleted, farming took over, and late in the twentieth century suburban growth from St. Paul added most of today's population.

The county covers 423 square miles, 9.1% of it water, which makes it the fourth smallest in the state by land. It holds 25 cities that lie wholly inside it, with Woodbury the largest, followed by Cottage Grove, Oakdale, Forest Lake and Stillwater. Census QuickFacts reports:

  • 286,895 people in July 2025, up 7.2% since the 2020 base
  • 115,270 housing units, 81.3% owner-occupied
  • A median owner-occupied value of $422,000, with $2,275 in monthly owner costs for homes with a mortgage
  • Median gross rent of $1,710 and median household income of $115,345
  • 2,382 building permits in 2025, and 49.1% of adults holding a bachelor's degree or higher

At those values a one percent shift in assessed value moves the tax bill by a meaningful sum, so the March valuation notice deserves a careful read before any listing decision.

sections.h2: What are the Washington County tax dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Most real estate is split into two equal payments. Agricultural land has its second half on November 15, manufactured homes pay on August 31 and November 15, and personal property is due in full May 15 for most owners. The October 15 deadline for an ordinary house passed a month ago. A proposed-tax notice, the Truth in Taxation notice, is mailed in mid-November, so it is reaching mailboxes now.

Non-homestead rates run higher, reaching 12% on the first half by October 1. Once January 2 passes, interest starts on unpaid tax, penalties and fees at an annual 8%, rising monthly. A third column in the county table covers owners who skipped both halves.

sections.h2: How does a Washington County appeal work?
sections.html:
Each spring the valuation notice rides in the same envelope as the tax statement, mailed by March 31. For 2026 the county asked owners to call the appraisers at 651-430-6175 first, since many questions end there. An in-person review of the property is required before any adjustment. After that the path depends on where the home sits.

  1. Cities and townships with a local board, such as Hugo (April 3), Forest Lake (April 14) and Lake Elmo (April 15) in 2026, expect you to appear if you want to keep the right to go further.
  2. Other places, including Woodbury, Stillwater, Oakdale and Cottage Grove, used four regional open book sessions in April, where attendance was optional.
  3. The County Board of Appeal and Equalization met June 17, 2026 at 5 p.m. at the Government Center, and an appointment was needed by May 1.
  4. The Minnesota Tax Court takes petitions through April 30 of the year taxes are payable.

A petition has to be served on the county auditor under section 278.01. Washington County prefers its online upload portal, which returns an acknowledgment of service within roughly 5 to 10 minutes. Email and fax are not accepted, and a petition left in the drop box is not service. Owners of income-producing property also owe disclosure documents by August 1.

sections.h2: What happens if Washington County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Tax unpaid after December 31 becomes delinquent on January 2, and the county starts proceedings in the spring with a letter and a published list of delinquent parcels. A $25 fee covers that notice. The first year of delinquency starts a three-year redemption period, and a property that is not redeemed forfeits to the State of Minnesota. The final notice adds a $150 fee and, according to the county, the sheriff delivers a copy to anyone living there.

A Confession of Judgment lets an owner, a lender, a contract for deed buyer or a life estate holder repay over time. The auditor assigns a ten-year plan for residential parcels with 10% down, or a five-year plan for commercial parcels with 20% down. The current year's tax and the yearly installment must both be paid by December 31 to stay in good standing.

sections.h2: Which Washington County relief programs affect a sale?
sections.html:
The homestead market value exclusion was increased beginning with taxes payable in 2025, and it shrinks as value rises. Non-homestead property carries higher penalty rates in the county table, so classification matters when a sale closes close to a deadline.

Two state refunds are described on the county page for owners who live in their property. The standard Property Tax Refund was open to households under $142,490 of 2025 income. The special refund requires a net tax increase of at least 12% and $100, and increases caused by improvements do not count. Forms and instructions are on the Minnesota Department of Revenue website.

sections.h2: How is tax settled when a Washington County house closes?
sections.html: The county's new homeowner page tells buyers to verify that tax due in the year of sale has been paid, giving the usual May 15 and October 15 halves. Under section 272.12 the auditor certifies delinquent tax before a deed is recorded. Ask the taxpayer services line for a payoff figure during the listing period, and have the title company show the year's split on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Washington County taxes in Woodbury instead of Stillwater?
faqs.a: Yes. The Woodbury service center on Woodlane Drive takes tax payments, as do the Cottage Grove and Forest Lake centers. A box payment is collected the next business day, so mail or pay online if the deadline is today.

faqs.q: What interest does Washington County charge on delinquent tax?
faqs.a: Interest runs at an annual rate of 8% on unpaid tax, penalties and fees beginning January 2, increasing monthly. Penalty percentages also step up on that date, so a balance grows quickly.

faqs.q: How do I serve a tax petition on Washington County?
faqs.a: Use the county's online petition portal, which returns an acknowledgment in a few minutes, or hand it to staff at the Government Center counter during business hours. Email and fax service are not agreed to, and the April 30 deadline is strict.

faqs.q: Is there a payment plan for back taxes in Washington County?
faqs.a: Yes, a Confession of Judgment. A residential parcel gets ten years with 10% down, and a commercial parcel gets five years with 20% down. The owner, a lender, a contract for deed buyer or a life estate holder may apply.

faqs.q: When did the Washington County Board of Appeal meet in 2026?
faqs.a: June 17, 2026 at 5 p.m. at the Government Center in Stillwater. Appointments had to be made by May 1 by calling 651-430-6175. Next year's dates appear on the valuation notice mailed in March.
